item.content: Mirror the error-handling conventions of sibling modules: reuse the same exception class and error codes (e.g. BillingError with codes like "invalid_state") and copy the exact message format used elsewhere (e.g. f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}") so behavior stays consistent.

When validating an integer parameter, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) since True/False are ints in Python, and reject non-int types like floats before comparing, so invalid input raises the domain error rather than slipping through.

After implementing, exercise edge cases manually (zero/negative/float/bool quantity, negative price, NaN, wrong invoice status) in addition to running the test suite, to confirm each validation path raises the expected error code.
